key_value.note: Flux-averaged CEvNS cross section on argon. Value 2.2e-39 cm^2 is the quote's (2.2 +/- 0.7) x 10^-39 cm^2 written in scientific notation; the +/-0.7e-39 in the display is the same quote's uncertainty.
key_value.quote: The measured cross section averaged over the incident neutrino flux is (2.2 +/- 0.7) x 10^-39 cm^2

name: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon

significance.quote: Two independent analyses prefer CEvNS over the background-only null hypothesis with greater than 3-sigma significance.

summary.plain: The first time neutrinos were caught bouncing gently off argon nuclei, using a 22-kilogram tank of liquid argon, confirming the effect follows the pattern the Standard Model predicts as the target nucleus changes.
summary.technical: First CEvNS measurement on argon using the 22 kg CENNS-10 liquid argon detector; two independent analyses each favor CEvNS over background-only at >3 sigma, with a flux-averaged cross section of (2.2+/-0.7)x10^-39 cm^2 consistent with the Standard Model, and combined with the CsI result to confirm the predicted neutron-number (N^2) scaling.

title: First Measurement of Coherent Elastic Neutrino-Nucleus Scattering on Argon
why_it_matters: Measuring CEvNS on a second target nucleus (argon, after CsI) tests the Standard Model's predicted N^2 dependence of the cross section on neutron number, directly relevant to the many current and future dark-matter and neutrino experiments that use liquid argon as a target.
